lens: product rubric + auth/security migration + public app release gate + CANON-019/031/041/045/048/051
primaryListVerdict: The empty Genius List hid one founder-authorized, live-verified auth migration. Obelisk OIDC is registered and operational, but direct activation would break Supabase UUID-based RLS. The ranked plan therefore implements a verified edge OIDC session, an explicit Obelisk-to-Supabase identity link, preserved member/investor onboarding, and truth-enforcing release gates as one migration.

items.title: Terminate Obelisk OIDC at the edge with PKCE, nonce, state, JWKS, and rotating sessions
items.why: The current callback is a Passport-era sessionStorage scaffold and does not implement the registered OIDC contract.
items.premise: The live issuer exposes discovery/JWKS and accepts the registered vaultsparkstudios-website authorization request, while the site still POSTs to /api/obelisk-verify.
liveEvidence: Live authorize request returns the Obelisk auth ceremony
Live discovery and ES256 JWKS return 200
cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js routes only the legacy verifier bridge
items.outcome: conversion: one passkey-first VaultSpark sign-in completes through a standards-bound, replay-resistant edge session without any site password.
items.recipe: Add a Worker-native OIDC handler using authorization-code plus PKCE S256; validate state, nonce, issuer, audience, kid, alg, signature, time claims, and verified email; keep tokens server-side in KV and rotate refresh tokens.

L2.recipe: Verify JWT and issue a server session.

L3.recipe: Fail closed on every OIDC invariant, rotate refresh tokens, bind redirects, and unit-test attack paths.

items.title: Bridge each Obelisk subject to the existing Supabase data identity without changing portal ownership
items.why: Member plans, ranks, investor rows, and dozens of RLS policies are keyed to Supabase auth UUIDs; replacing that UUID would orphan production data.
items.premise: The live project has 233 Supabase users, zero Obelisk mappings, and pervasive auth.uid() policies.
liveEvidence: Supabase admin inventory: 233 UUID users and zero obelisk_sub mappings
investors.user_id references auth.users(id)
vault_members and portal RPCs use auth.uid()
items.outcome: conversion: every existing member or investor reaches the same portal record after Obelisk sign-in, while new users receive a data-only UUID automatically.
items.recipe: Add a service-role-only identity link table, resolve existing users by verified email, create data-only shadow users for new identities, mint a short-lived Supabase compatibility session, and make the operation idempotent.

L2.recipe: Link existing users and create shadow users.

L3.recipe: Preserve UUID continuity, handle conflicts fail-closed, mint compatibility sessions, and prove idempotency.

items.title: Make Obelisk the only authority while retaining Supabase as a transparent RLS transport
items.why: A legacy browser Supabase session can currently outlive any Obelisk state, so a superficial provider flip would leave two competing identities.
items.premise: assets/supabase-client.js creates and trusts persisted Supabase sessions before identity.js loads.
liveEvidence: activeProvider is supabase
portal pages call VSSupabase.auth.getSession directly
supabase-client.js persists its own browser session
items.outcome: conversion + info-finding: portal code waits for one canonical Obelisk-backed bootstrap, and an absent/revoked Obelisk session clears any stale compatibility token.
items.recipe: Bootstrap the browser client from /api/auth/session, gate getSession until completion, disable password/OAuth entry points, clear legacy-only state, and expose a normalized Obelisk identity plus Supabase-compatible raw session.

L1.recipe: Fetch and set the bridge session.

L2.recipe: Gate direct getSession calls and sign-out both layers.

L3.recipe: Eliminate legacy-session bypasses, normalize events, and test timing/revocation paths.

items.title: Replace member passwords with an Obelisk ceremony while preserving Vault Handle, invite, newsletter, rank, and plan onboarding
items.why: The create-account surface currently asks for a second password and falsely labels Obelisk as coming later.
items.premise: Member registration calls Supabase signUp before register_open; the existing OAuth completion panel already provides the correct post-identity profile seam.
liveEvidence: vault-member/index.html contains password/reset/social provider UI
portal-auth.js signs up with Supabase then calls register_open
portal-settings.js already detects authenticated users missing vault_members rows
items.outcome: conversion: members create or enter one VaultSpark account through Obelisk, then complete only VaultSpark-specific profile choices inside the preserved member portal.
items.recipe: Replace password/social forms with Obelisk sign-in/create actions and live seal, reuse the completion panel for handle/invite/subscription, call register_open after the compatibility session exists, and retain all dashboard logic.

L3.recipe: Polish both themes/mobile states, referral carry, errors, accessibility, and no-password copy.

items.title: Move investor sign-in and account creation to Obelisk without flattening the investor application workflow
items.why: Investor access is a business role, not a second identity system; its application, approval, tier, consent, and audit trail must remain specific to VaultSpark.
items.premise: The login page owns password auth but investor-auth.js correctly validates portal authorization after session establishment.
liveEvidence: Investor login uses VSIdentity but that provider is Supabase
get_my_investor_profile remains the authorization source
investor application data is stored separately in investor_requests
items.outcome: conversion: investors use the same Obelisk identity as members while the VaultSpark application and approval gate remain intact and confidential.
items.recipe: Replace sign-in/reset/password UX with Obelisk, preserve and submit the application before signup redirect, maintain next-route validation, and keep investor RPC authorization unchanged.

L3.recipe: Carry return state safely, polish status messaging, and test approved/pending/rejected/admin branches.

items.title: Verify private-portal sessions at the edge instead of checking cookie presence
items.why: The current edge gate treats any cookie with the expected name as authentication and includes the public investor login route in the gated prefix.
liveEvidence: GATED_PATH_PATTERNS matches all investor-portal paths
Layer 2 checks presence only
portalGateRedirect points every private path to the member page
items.outcome: security + conversion: forged/stale cookies do not open private shells, and unauthenticated investors land on their own Obelisk entry page without loops.
items.recipe: Cryptographically verify the session-id cookie and KV record, exempt public auth routes, preserve safe return paths, and route member/admin/investor gates to the right entry surface.

L2.recipe: Validate KV expiry and fix redirects.

L3.recipe: Cover tamper, expiry, missing KV, login-loop, and open-redirect cases.

items.title: Replace the scaffold checker with a behavioral Obelisk activation contract
items.why: The build currently passes only when it proves Obelisk is not active, making the observability surface structurally incapable of telling the new truth.
items.premise: check-obelisk-passport-contract.mjs asserts activeProvider=supabase and prints scaffold present; activation explicitly not claimed.
liveEvidence: The checker rejects providerFlip
build:check runs the checker
STARTUP_BRIEF truth signal repeats the scaffold posture
items.outcome: info-finding: builds fail unless OIDC, identity linking, session authority, both portals, and no-password UX agree on the same active architecture.
items.recipe: Rewrite the contract gate around behavioral invariants and negative fixtures; add pure Worker auth tests and a live discovery/authorize smoke that remains honest when the issuer is unavailable.

L2.recipe: Assert the bridge and both portal surfaces.

L3.recipe: Prove attack/failure paths and distinguish local contract from live-provider availability.

items.title: Turn account settings into a clear identity-versus-membership control plane
items.why: Once Obelisk owns credentials, password controls in VaultSpark settings become misleading, but users still need an obvious place to manage security and a separate place to manage their Vault identity and plan.
items.premise: Member settings currently exposes local password semantics while the canonical handoff says all credential management belongs to Obelisk.
liveEvidence: portal-settings.js listens for Supabase password recovery
Obelisk Gate owns passkeys, TOTP, recovery, devices, and account-security email
VaultSpark owns handle, profile, plan, and investor roles
items.outcome: info-finding: users can immediately tell what Obelisk secures and what VaultSpark membership controls, with direct routes to each plane.
items.recipe: Add a concise Security by Obelisk card and account-management link, remove local password controls, preserve profile/plan controls, and use precise non-hype language.

L3.recipe: Integrate assurance/status semantics accessibly across both portals.

items.title: Apply the identity schema and ship a rollback-safe staging proof before production
items.why: An auth implementation that exists only in git is not functional, and a production flip without schema/secrets/staging evidence would be reckless.
items.premise: The database and Worker require new runtime state, while this SPARKED app has a mandatory Hetzner staging gate.
liveEvidence: supabase.admin and cloudflare.deploy capabilities are present
stagingType is hetzner
previous Worker token probes reported an R2-bound resource scope risk
items.outcome: conversion + operations: the migration reaches a verifiable environment with an additive rollback path, direct exit-code evidence, and no fabricated green state.
items.recipe: Apply the additive SQL through the secrets gateway, configure Worker secrets, deploy and smoke staging, run member/investor browser paths, then promote only if every release gate is green.

L3.recipe: Run live OIDC, portal-role, mobile, rollback, security, and deploy-currency evidence.

skipped.reason: Rejected after live verification: existing auth.uid() policies and UUID foreign keys cannot consume an opaque Obelisk subject without a compatibility identity.

Rejected for this registration: the canonical Obelisk relying party is a secretless public OIDC client with a direct site callback, while Supabase custom OIDC configuration expects its own callback/client configuration and would make Supabase the visible broker again.
Rejected by founder direction and CANON-045: keeping public Supabase password entry would leave two identity authorities and make the migration claim false.
Rejected: cost is notional flat-rate Max Plan and the auth flow is self-hosted/cost-neutral; no alarm is justified.

honestyLedger.title: A provider flag flip was refused
honestyLedger.why: It would strand member and investor data behind UUID-based RLS.

honestyLedger.title: Supabase remains, but not as identity
honestyLedger.why: It is retained only as the existing data/authorization transport until those policies are deliberately migrated; describing it as removed would be false.

honestyLedger.title: Live provider health is not a full end-to-end pass
honestyLedger.why: Discovery, JWKS, verification card, and authorize redirect are live; callback and portal continuity still require this implementation and a real account ceremony.

notes: All nine items are one migration surface. Every premise is backed by live issuer behavior, current repository code, current Supabase schema, or gateway-probed inventory. Every item names a conversion or information-finding outcome.
